title: DIMS dashboard config.json
description: Describes one study. Written by hand or by the builder, read by the dashboard and by every analysis step. Before this schema existed there were three mutually incompatible dialects in use; keys marked 'tab-owned' come from tabs that were built in separate forks.

pairList.description: Either explicit pairs [[a,b],[a,c]], or a legacy flat list [a,b,c] which is expanded to all combinations. Both forms are supported; prefer pairs. anyOf, not oneOf: an empty list is valid under both branches, and oneOf would reject it.

videoIDs.description: Session identifiers. Each must have assets/videos/{videoID}.mp4 unless a videoSrcTemplate is set.

dataTypes.description: Per video, the measures available. Each implies assets/timeseries/{videoID}_{dataType}.csv.

include_RQA.description: Data types to run recurrence quantification on. Empty or absent disables the tab.

defaultWindowSize.description: Half-width, in seconds, of the window around the playhead.

perspectives.description: tab-owned (video): named camera angles, e.g. wide/parent/child.

videoPerspectives.description: tab-owned (video): which perspectives exist per video.

fallbackVideoSrcTemplate.description: tab-owned (video): used when the chosen perspective is missing.

trajectory_settings.description: tab-owned (trajectory): background image and field geometry.

path_images.description: tab-owned (trajectory): image extent in field coordinates.

analysis.description: Per-analysis tuning, keyed by step id. Exists so a study can change a parameter without maintaining its own copy of an analysis script -- which is what one fork previously had to do. Units here are always seconds, never multiples of the sampling interval.

maxPeriod.description: Longest period to compute, in seconds.

include_network.description: study-owned (case-karnatak): the cross-effector coherence graph. The tab lives in that study's tabs/ directory, not in the core, because it reads node identities out of data type names (person + body part) and means nothing to a study that names its measures differently.
